chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Ẓarīf narrated to me.

He said: Two questions stirred within my chest, and I wanted to write concerning them to Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام). So I wrote asking him about al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام): when he rises, by what will he judge, and where will be his assembly in which he judges among the people? And I had wanted to ask him about something for quartan fever, but I omitted mention of the fever.

Then the reply came: You asked about al-Qāʾim; when he rises, he will judge among the people by his knowledge, like the judgment of Dāwūd (عليه السلام), and he will not ask for evidence. And you had wanted to ask about quartan fever, but you were made to forget; so write on a sheet and hang it upon the fever-stricken person, and he will recover by the permission of Allah, if Allah wills.
O fire, be coolness and peace upon Ibrāhīm.
So we hung upon him what Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) had mentioned, and he recovered.

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: formal proof or evidentiary proof presented in disputes
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: al-Qāʾim, the awaited Imam whose future rise is being asked about
key_terms.الْمَحْمُومِ: the fever-stricken person upon whom the written text is hung
key_terms.بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا: coolness and peace, the Qur'anic phrase used here for healing
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: by the permission of Allah, expressing that healing occurs only through divine leave
key_terms.بِعِلْمِهِ: by his knowledge, meaning his direct authoritative knowledge in judgment
key_terms.حُمَّى الرِّبْعِ: quartan fever, a recurring fever mentioned in the question
key_terms.كَقَضَاءِ دَاوُدَ: like the judgment of Dāwūd, indicating judgment without reliance on outward evidence

ai.seo_question: How will al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام) judge among the people, and what remedy is mentioned here for quartan fever?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a written question to Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) about al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام) and a forgotten inquiry about quartan fever. The response states that al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام) will judge by divinely granted knowledge like Dāwūd (عليه السلام), and it also provides a Qur'anic healing inscription that was used and brought recovery by Allah’s permission.
